headline_marked: Two [[BNP leaders killed]] in separate attacks in Kishoreganj and Noakhali
headline: Two BNP leaders killed in separate attacks in Kishoreganj and Noakhali
summary: Police have arrested suspects in both cases; one victim allegedly protested against drug trading in his area.
details: Two local BNP leaders were stabbed to death in separate incidents in Kishoreganj and Noakhali on Wednesday night.
In Kishoreganj, Jahidul Alam, 52, former president of Mithamoin upazila BNP, was ambushed and murdered outside his home. A party activist accompanying him was injured in the attack.
Police have arrested one suspect in the Kishoreganj case. The motive behind the attack remains under investigation.
In Noakhali, Md Faruk, 55, former publicity secretary of Ward No. 6 BNP, was stabbed from behind while drinking tea at a stall near Tetultala Bazar.
Faruk's family alleges he was killed for protesting against illegal drug trading and abuse in the area, following an altercation with a known drug dealer.
Locals caught two suspects in Noakhali and handed them over to the police. Investigations into both killings are ongoing.

Police have arrested one suspect in the Kishoreganj case. The motive behind the attack remains under investigation.

In Noakhali, Md Faruk, 55, former publicity secretary of Ward No. 6 BNP, was stabbed from behind while drinking tea at a stall near Tetultala Bazar.

Faruk's family alleges he was killed for protesting against illegal drug trading and abuse in the area, following an altercation with a known drug dealer.

Locals caught two suspects in Noakhali and handed them over to the police. Investigations into both killings are ongoing.

headline_marked: Waterlogged [[Oxygen-Kuwaish road in Chattogram turns into a swamp]]
headline: Waterlogged Oxygen-Kuwaish road in Chattogram turns into a swamp
summary: Commuters face extreme hardship as hidden potholes under stagnant water cause vehicles to break down and risk accidents on the 5km stretch.
details: The Oxygen-Kuwaish road in Chattogram's Ananya Residential Area has become a nightmare for commuters, with large potholes hidden under stagnant water causing vehicles to stall and break down.

A CNG-run autorickshaw driver, Hafizur Rahman, reported that his engine stopped twice after falling into deep holes that were invisible due to the waterlogging, describing the feeling as pushing a vehicle through a swamp.
The 5km road was built by the Chittagong Development Authority (CDA) at a cost of 45 crore BDT and was opened for traffic in January 2016.
Despite being open for nearly a decade, the road has not been handed over to the Chattogram City Corporation (CCC) due to a dispute over its poor condition.
The CCC refuses to take over the road, arguing that it must be be in usable condition before handover, as repairing it now would cost as much as rebuilding it from scratch.
The road serves thousands of daily users, including students and office-goers from Hathazari, Rauzan, and Kaptai, as well as residents of the area's hospitals and schools.
A joint committee recommended in January that the CDA either rebuild the road before handover or provide the necessary funds to the City Corporation for reconstruction.
CDA Chairman Belayet Hossain stated that maintenance work has been hampered by heavy rains, but the road will be handed over to the CCC once the work is completed.
